CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding (positive Lyme titer).

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Michelle is a 31-year-old female with past medical history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension who presents with a positive Lyme titer. She reports an insect bite approximately two weeks ago while hiking in the woods. She describes fatigue and lack of energy, swollen joints in both elbows with associated pain, body aches, nausea, and poor appetite, eating mainly toast and crackers. She notes a bull's-eye rash. She denies high fevers. Regarding her diabetes, she reports blood sugars have been okay with occasional highs and lows but nothing significantly out of range. She denies abdominal pain and diarrhea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses nausea, joint pain, and body aches. Denies abdominal pain, diarrhea, and high fevers.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin
Lisinopril

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Went hiking in the woods approximately two weeks ago. Monitors blood pressure at home using a cuff purchased last year. Avoids salty foods.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Normal, no fever. Bilateral elbow joint swelling with pain to palpation. Bull's-eye rash on left side of abdomen, warm to palpation, non-tender to palpation, no evidence of cellulitis. Heart and lungs: normal. Remainder of exam: normal.

RESULTS
Lyme titer: Elevated. Complete laboratory workup: normal, no elevated white blood cell count.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Newly diagnosed Lyme disease: Prescribe doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for three weeks. Consult with infectious disease. Follow-up appointment next week.

2. Type 2 diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c. Continue metformin.

3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Order lipid panel. Continue home blood pressure monitoring. Refill lisinopril prescription.
